title: finding(plugin-calendar): ObjectCalendar's pull-to-refresh never arms on the internal-fetch path — the mount effect runs while the ref is still null
body:
Path: P2 | 那条路第 2 步「本地跑起来、看到」 | 内部取数路径上 `ObjectCalendar` 的下拉刷新从不挂载 —— 首帧是 loading,effect 跑时 ref 还是 null
分诊重测与定级:2026-09-20T15:59Z

Dedupe words: `usePullToRefresh listeners never attached` · `pull to refresh dead on first render` · `mount effect ref null loading screen` · `ObjectCalendar internal fetch gesture` · `pullRef null when effect runs`

Reproduced by the objectui#10031 dev **while writing that card's pin**, ⛔ not inferred. ⚠️ **Marked 转述 in part** — see the split below. ⛔ No `priority:*` / `type`: the triage seat's sole production. `domain:ui` inherited from the in-flight parent objectui#10031.

## The claim

`ObjectCalendar`'s **pull-to-refresh gesture never arms on the internal-fetch path.** `usePullToRefresh` attaches its native listeners in a **mount effect** whose dependencies are all stable for this component (`enabled` constant; `onRefresh` a `useCallback` with an empty dependency list) — and on the internal-fetch path the **first render is the loading screen**, so the ref is `null` when the effect runs and the effect never re-runs.

⇒ driving the gesture through the internal fetch produces **nothing**. The same gesture through **pre-fetched** data works — which is the route the new objectui#10031 pin takes, and it says so at the assertion.

## ⭐ What this seat measured and what it did not

- **自量**: the hook IS wired into this component — `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx:28` imports `usePullToRefresh` from `@object-ui/mobile` and `:408` destructures `{ ref: pullRef, isRefreshing, pullDistance }` from it. So the feature is declared present, ⛔ not vestigial.
- ⚠️ **转述, ⛔ NOT re-run by this seat**: the mount-effect/null-ref mechanism inside `@object-ui/mobile`, and the 「works with pre-fetched data, dead on internal fetch」 asymmetry. ⇒ ⭐ **the taking dev re-takes this leg first**, with both arms in one run (internal-fetch path and pre-fetched path), because the asymmetry IS the finding and a single-arm reading cannot show it.

## Why it is class (a) and not a cosmetic gap

A declared, shipped affordance that silently does nothing on the path most users take. ⛔ No error, ⛔ no warning, ⛔ no visual hint — the user pulls and the list does not refresh, and nothing names a cause. The user-visible half is the whole defect.

⚠️ **The fix shape is ⛔ not decided here.** Re-running the effect when the ref attaches, deferring the gesture until data renders, and rendering the scroll container before the loading screen are all plausible and they differ in cost and in blast radius — the one that also changes what renders during loading is a product-visible change and should be said out loud rather than slipped in.

## ⛔ What this card does NOT claim

- ⛔ Not that `usePullToRefresh` is broken. Its other consumers are unmeasured here; this is about how THIS component mounts.
- ⛔ Not that objectui#10031 should have fixed it: it was fenced to that card's surface, and it reported the reproduction rather than reaching out of it.

## Acceptance

- The asymmetry is re-measured first-hand, both arms in one run, with the file state verified in the same command.
- A pin that drives the gesture on the **internal-fetch** path goes RED before the fix and GREEN after; the pre-fetched arm stays green throughout as the lit control, ⛔ so a fix that breaks both cannot read as success.
- If the chosen repair changes what renders during loading, that is stated in the PR body as a product-visible change, ⛔ not left to be discovered.
